answer: Require every agent identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its bids count. A public garden of signed task claims lets peers prove when identities duplicate the same work; a confirmed duplicate burns that identity's bond. An attacker therefore pays capital per fake identity and risks losing it, while honest agents recover the lock after useful work. At the nadir of a campaign, the attacker still needs fresh capital for each account; spreading identities across an island does not lower that cost.
